problem.summary: 3D形状识别中，应使用原生3D表示（如体素网格、多边形网格）还是基于视图的描述符？

motivation.summary: 传统3D形状描述符（如SPH、LFD）是手工设计的，维度高且易过拟合；而基于视图的描述符维度低、计算高效、对3D表示伪影鲁棒。现有3D数据集有限，但2D图像数据集（如ImageNet）庞大，可迁移学习。

core_idea.summary: 使用2D渲染视图的卷积神经网络（CNN）来识别3D形状，甚至单视图就能超越基于3D表示的方法；进一步提出多视图CNN（MVCNN）架构，通过视图池化层聚合多视图信息，生成紧凑的3D形状描述符。

method.summary: 1. 输入：从多边形网格渲染多视图图像（两种相机设置）。2. 基线：使用预训练CNN（如VGG）提取单视图特征，用SVM分类或平均最小距离检索。3. MVCNN：多视图共享CNN1，经视图池化层（逐元素最大值）聚合，再通过CNN2生成形状描述符。4. 可选：使用低秩马氏度量学习进一步优化描述符。

experiments.summary: 在ModelNet40数据集上评估分类和检索任务；在SketchClean数据集上评估草图识别；在自建草图-3D形状数据集上评估草图检索。

claims.claim: 1. 基于视图的2D表示能有效识别3D形状，甚至单视图就优于基于3D表示的方法。2. 多视图CNN（MVCNN）通过视图池化聚合多视图信息，生成更紧凑、更准确的形状描述符。3. MVCNN可应用于草图识别和草图检索任务。

limitations.limitation: 1. 依赖渲染视图的质量和相机设置。2. 未探索最优视图数量或动态视图选择。3. 草图检索性能仍有提升空间（如通过度量学习）。

nodes.title: 多视图渲染
nodes.label: 输入生成
nodes.summary: 从3D多边形网格渲染多个2D视图图像，作为CNN的输入。
nodes.description: 使用Phong反射模型渲染多边形网格。两种相机设置：1) 假设形状直立，12个视图，相机每30度放置，仰角30度；2) 不假设直立，80个视图，从二十面体顶点放置。渲染每个网格耗时不超过10毫秒。

nodes.title: 单视图CNN特征提取
nodes.label: 基线方法
nodes.summary: 使用预训练CNN（如VGG）提取单个视图的图像特征（如fc7层）。
nodes.description: 网络在ImageNet上预训练，然后在3D形状的渲染视图上微调。使用fc7层（ReLU后，4096维）作为图像描述符。

nodes.title: 视图池化层
nodes.label: 核心创新
nodes.summary: 在MVCNN中，对多个视图的特征图进行逐元素最大值池化，聚合多视图信息。
nodes.description: 视图池化层可放置在网络中的不同位置，实验表明放置在最后一个卷积层（conv5）附近效果最佳。与最大池化层和maxout层相关，但池化维度不同。

nodes.title: MVCNN架构
nodes.label: 完整模型
nodes.summary: 多视图CNN：多视图共享CNN1，经视图池化后通过CNN2，生成紧凑的3D形状描述符。
nodes.description: 每个视图独立通过CNN1（共享参数），在视图池化层聚合，然后通过CNN2。使用fc7层（ReLU后）作为聚合形状描述符。可训练或微调。

nodes.title: 分类与检索
nodes.label: 任务应用
nodes.summary: 使用形状描述符进行3D形状分类（线性SVM）和检索（平均最小距离）。
nodes.description: 分类：训练一对多线性SVM，测试时对多视图预测取平均。检索：使用平均最小距离度量（公式1）。MVCNN描述符可直接用于比较3D形状。

nodes.title: 度量学习
nodes.label: 可选优化
nodes.summary: 使用低秩马氏度量学习进一步优化MVCNN输出的形状描述符。
nodes.description: 使用大间隔度量学习算法，将描述符投影到低维空间（p=128），使同类形状距离小，异类距离大。

nodes.title: 草图识别与检索
nodes.label: 扩展应用
nodes.summary: 将MVCNN应用于手绘草图识别和草图-3D形状检索。
nodes.description: 草图识别：使用数据抖动（增强）生成多视图，通过MVCNN聚合。草图检索：将3D形状渲染为线图风格（Canny边缘检测），与草图描述符比较。

edges.label: 输入
edges.description: 渲染的多视图图像作为单视图CNN的输入。

edges.label: 输入
edges.description: 渲染的多视图图像作为MVCNN的输入。

edges.label: 特征输入
edges.description: 单视图CNN特征用于分类和检索基线。

edges.label: 集成
edges.description: 视图池化层是MVCNN架构的核心组件。

edges.label: 描述符输出
edges.description: MVCNN生成的形状描述符用于分类和检索。

edges.label: 描述符输入
edges.description: MVCNN描述符可进一步通过度量学习优化。

edges.label: 模型应用
edges.description: MVCNN架构应用于草图识别和检索任务。

deltas.before: 使用手工设计的3D形状描述符（如SPH、LFD）或基于体素的深度学习（3D ShapeNets）。
deltas.after: 使用基于2D渲染视图的CNN特征，甚至单视图就超越3D方法。
deltas.why_it_matters: 证明了2D视图表示的有效性，利用了大规模2D图像数据集（ImageNet）的预训练优势，避免了3D数据稀缺和维度灾难问题。

deltas.before: 使用单视图CNN特征，通过平均最小距离或多视图预测平均进行聚合。
deltas.after: 使用MVCNN通过视图池化层学习聚合多视图信息，生成单一描述符。
deltas.why_it_matters: 生成了更紧凑、更高效的描述符，避免了成对距离计算，显著提升了检索性能（mAP从62.8%提升到70.1%）。

deltas.before: 视图池化层位置未优化。
deltas.after: 实验发现视图池化层应放置在最后一个卷积层（conv5）附近以获得最佳性能。
deltas.why_it_matters: 提供了架构设计指导，确保多视图信息在适当抽象层次聚合。

deltas.before: 形状描述符维度较高（如fc7的4096维）。
deltas.after: 可选使用低秩马氏度量学习将描述符投影到低维空间（p=128）。
deltas.why_it_matters: 使描述符更紧凑，同时可能提升判别性。

variables.name: x
variables.description: 一个3D形状的多视图表示，包含n_x个视图特征向量x_i。

variables.name: y
variables.description: 另一个3D形状的多视图表示，包含n_y个视图特征向量y_j。

variables.name: d(x, y)
variables.description: 两个3D形状x和y之间的对称平均最小距离。

formulas.intuition: 计算两个3D形状之间的距离：对于形状x的每个视图，找到形状y中最相似的视图，取距离；反之亦然；然后对称平均。这确保了距离度量的对称性。

formulas.latex: [w_1, w_2, ..., w_K] = \left[ \frac{\partial F_c}{\partial I_1}\bigg|_S, \frac{\partial F_c}{\partial I_2}\bigg|_S, ..., \frac{\partial F_c}{\partial I_K}\bigg|_S \right]

variables.name: F_c
variables.description: 网络输出层（如fc8）对于真实类别c的分数。

variables.name: w_k
variables.description: 视图I_k的梯度能量，表示该视图对类别分数F_c的影响程度。

formulas.intuition: 通过反向传播计算类别分数对每个视图图像的梯度，得到每个视图的显著性权重。权重大的视图对分类决策更重要。

main_result.description: 在ModelNet40数据集上，MVCNN（微调，12视图）达到89.9%分类准确率和70.1%检索mAP，显著优于所有基线（包括3D ShapeNets的77.3%和单视图CNN的85.1%）。

ablation.description: 1. 视图池化层位置：conv5附近最佳，早于conv4性能显著下降。2. 视图池化操作：逐元素最大值优于平均值。3. 微调：在ModelNet40上微调显著提升性能。4. 视图数量：单视图已优于3D方法，多视图进一步提升。

robustness.description: 1. 相机设置：两种设置（12视图直立假设 vs 80视图无假设）均有效，后者性能略降但依然强劲。2. 渲染：光照模型变化不影响描述符，因CNN滤波器对光照不变。

scaling.description: 视图数量从1增加到12，分类和检索性能持续提升。但未探索更多视图（如80）在MVCNN上的效果（仅用于无直立假设设置）。

case_study.description: 1. 草图识别：在SketchClean数据集上，MVCNN（微调，6视图抖动）达到87.2%准确率，优于CNN基线（86.3%）。2. 草图检索：在自建数据集上，MVCNN（未微调）达到36.1% mAP。

human_eval.description: 草图识别任务中，人类准确率为93.0%，MVCNN达到87.2%，接近人类水平。

benchmark.description: 主要基准：ModelNet40（分类和检索）、SketchClean（草图识别）、自建草图-3D形状数据集（草图检索）。

efficiency.description: 1. 渲染效率：每个网格渲染所有视图耗时不超过10毫秒。2. 描述符效率：MVCNN生成单一描述符，避免了成对距离计算，比多视图基线更高效。

experiments.description: 在ModelNet40数据集上，MVCNN（微调，12视图）达到89.9%分类准确率和70.1%检索mAP，显著优于所有基线（包括3D ShapeNets的77.3%和单视图CNN的85.1%）。
experiments.name: main_result_1
experiments.result_summary: MVCNN achieves 89.9% classification accuracy and 70.1% retrieval mAP on ModelNet40, outperforming all baselines.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: MVCNN with fine-tuning and multiple views significantly outperforms existing 3D shape descriptors and view-based baselines.

experiments.description: 1. 视图池化层位置：conv5附近最佳，早于conv4性能显著下降。2. 视图池化操作：逐元素最大值优于平均值。3. 微调：在ModelNet40上微调显著提升性能。4. 视图数量：单视图已优于3D方法，多视图进一步提升。
experiments.name: ablation_2
experiments.result_summary: Ablation studies show optimal view-pooling placement at conv5, superiority of max pooling, benefits of fine-tuning, and performance gains from multiple views.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: Key design choices in MVCNN architecture and training procedure are validated through ablation experiments.

experiments.description: 1. 相机设置：两种设置（12视图直立假设 vs 80视图无假设）均有效，后者性能略降但依然强劲。2. 渲染：光照模型变化不影响描述符，因CNN滤波器对光照不变。
experiments.name: robustness_3
experiments.result_summary: MVCNN is robust to different camera setups and illumination models due to CNN filter invariance.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: The method is robust to variations in rendering setup and illumination.

experiments.description: 视图数量从1增加到12，分类和检索性能持续提升。但未探索更多视图（如80）在MVCNN上的效果（仅用于无直立假设设置）。
experiments.name: scaling_4
experiments.result_summary: Performance improves with more views from 1 to 12, but effect of more views (e.g., 80) on MVCNN not explored.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: Multiple views provide additional information that improves recognition performance.

experiments.description: 1. 草图识别：在SketchClean数据集上，MVCNN（微调，6视图抖动）达到87.2%准确率，优于CNN基线（86.3%）。2. 草图检索：在自建数据集上，MVCNN（未微调）达到36.1% mAP。
experiments.name: case_study_5
experiments.result_summary: MVCNN achieves 87.2% accuracy on SketchClean and 36.1% mAP on sketch-based 3D shape retrieval.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: MVCNN can be applied to sketch recognition and sketch-based 3D shape retrieval tasks.

experiments.description: 草图识别任务中，人类准确率为93.0%，MVCNN达到87.2%，接近人类水平。
experiments.name: human_eval_6
experiments.result_summary: MVCNN achieves 87.2% accuracy compared to human performance of 93.0% on sketch recognition.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: MVCNN performance approaches human-level accuracy on sketch recognition.

experiments.description: 主要基准：ModelNet40（分类和检索）、SketchClean（草图识别）、自建草图-3D形状数据集（草图检索）。
experiments.name: benchmark_7
experiments.result_summary: Three benchmark datasets are used for evaluation: ModelNet40 for 3D shape classification/retrieval, SketchClean for sketch recognition, and a custom dataset for sketch-based retrieval.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: The method is evaluated on standard and custom benchmarks covering different tasks.

experiments.description: 1. 渲染效率：每个网格渲染所有视图耗时不超过10毫秒。2. 描述符效率：MVCNN生成单一描述符，避免了成对距离计算，比多视图基线更高效。
experiments.name: efficiency_8
experiments.result_summary: Rendering is fast (<10ms per mesh) and MVCNN produces compact descriptors enabling efficient comparison.
experiments.what_it_tries_to_prove: The method is computationally efficient for both rendering and descriptor computation.

terms.definition: 从多个虚拟相机视角渲染3D形状得到的一组2D图像。
MVCNN中的特殊层，对多个视图的特征图进行逐元素最大值（或平均值）池化，以聚合多视图信息。
多视图卷积神经网络，通过共享CNN1、视图池化层和CNN2，将多视图信息聚合为单一形状描述符。
公式1中定义的对称距离度量，用于比较两个多视图表示的3D形状。
数据增强技术，通过对图像进行变换（如平移、翻转、颜色扰动）生成额外样本，用于训练或测试时提升鲁棒性。
通过反向传播计算类别分数对输入图像的梯度，可视化每个像素对分类决策的影响程度。

steps.description: 1. 数据准备：下载ModelNet40数据集，按论文划分训练/测试集。
2. 渲染多视图：使用Phong反射模型渲染3D网格，生成12视图（直立假设）或80视图（无假设）图像。
3. 训练基线CNN：在ImageNet上预训练VGG网络，然后在渲染视图上微调。
4. 实现MVCNN：构建共享CNN1、视图池化层（逐元素最大值）、CNN2的架构。
5. 训练MVCNN：使用微调后的CNN1初始化，在ModelNet40上端到端微调整个MVCNN。
6. 评估：使用线性SVM进行分类，使用平均最小距离进行检索。
7. 可选：实现低秩马氏度量学习优化描述符。
8. 扩展应用：实现草图识别（数据抖动）和草图检索（线图渲染）。

metadata.title: Multi-view Convolutional Neural Networks for 3D Shape Recognition
metadata.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: A longstanding question in computer vision concerns the representation of 3D shapes for recognition: should 3D shapes be represented with descriptors operating on their native 3D formats, such as voxel grid or polygon mesh, or can they be effectively represented with view-based descriptors? We address this question in the context of learning to recognize 3D shapes from a collection of their rendered views on 2D images. We first present a standard CNN architecture trained to recognize the shapes' rendered views independently of each other, and show that a 3D shape can be recognized even from a single view at an accuracy far higher than using state-of-the-art 3D shape descriptors. Recognition rates further increase when multiple views of the shapes are provided. In addition, we present a novel CNN architecture that combines information from multiple views of a 3D shape into a single and compact shape descriptor offering even better recognition performance. The same architecture can be applied to accurately recognize human hand-drawn sketches of shapes. We conclude that a collection of 2D views can be highly informative for 3D shape recognition and is amenable to emerging CNN architectures and their derivatives.

Shape descriptors. A large corpus of shape descriptors

has been developed for drawing inferences about 3D objects in both the computer vision and graphics literature. Shape descriptors can be classiﬁed into two broad categories: 3D shape descriptors that directly work on the native 3D repre- sentations of objects, such as polygon meshes, voxel-based discretizations, point clouds, or implicit surfaces, and view- based descriptors that describe the shape of a 3D object by “how it looks” in a collection of 2D projections. With the exception of the recent work of Wu et al. [37] which learns shape descriptors from the voxel-based repre- sentation of an object through 3D convolutional nets, pre-
vious 3D shape descriptors were largely “hand-designed”

according to a particular geometric property of the shape surface or volume. For example, shapes can be represented with histograms or bag-of-features models constructed out of surface normals and curvatures [15], distances, angles, triangle areas or tetrahedra volumes gathered at sampled surface points [25], properties of spherical functions deﬁned in volumetric grids [16], local shape diameters measured at densely sampled surface points [4], heat kernel signatures on polygon meshes [2, 19], or extensions of the SIFT and SURF feature descriptors to 3D voxel grids [17]. Develop- ing classiﬁers and other supervised machine learning algo- rithms on top of such 3D shape descriptors poses a number of challenges. First, the size of organized databases with annotated 3D models is rather limited compared to image datasets, e.g., ModelNet contains about 150K shapes (its 40 category benchmark contains about 4K shapes). In contrast, the ImageNet database [9] already includes tens of millions of...

be very high-dimensional, making classiﬁers prone to over- ﬁtting due to the so-called ‘curse of dimensionality’. On the other hand view-based descriptors have a number of desirable properties: they are relatively low-dimensional, efﬁcient to evaluate, and robust to 3D shape representation artifacts, such as holes, imperfect polygon mesh tessela- tions, noisy surfaces. The rendered shape views can also be directly compared with other 2D images, silhouettes or even hand-drawn sketches. An early example of a view-based approach is the work by Murase and Nayar [24] that rec- ognizes objects by matching their appearance in parametric
eigenspaces formed by large sets of 2D renderings of 3D
models under varying poses and illuminations. Another ex-

ample, which is particularly popular in computer graphics setups, is the LightField descriptor [5] that extracts a set of geometric and Fourier descriptors from object silhouettes rendered from several different viewpoints. Alternatively, the silhouette of an object can be decomposed into parts and then represented by a directed acyclic graph (shock graph) [23]. Cyr and Kimia [8] deﬁned similarity metrics based on curve matching and grouped similar views, called aspect graphs of 3D models [18]. Eitz et al. [12] compared human sketches with line drawings of 3D models produced from several different views based on local Gabor ﬁlters, while Schneider et al. [30] proposed using Fisher vectors [26] on SIFT features [22] for representing human sketches of
shapes. These descriptors are largely “hand-engineered”
and some do not generalize well across different domains. Convolutional neural networks. Our work is also related to recent advances in image recognition using CNNs [20].
In particular CNNs trained on the large datasets such as

ImageNet have been shown to learn general purpose im- age descriptors for a number of vision tasks such as object detection, scene recognition, texture recognition and ﬁne- grained classiﬁcation [10, 13, 28, 7]. We show that these deep architectures can be adapted to speciﬁc domains in- cluding shaded illustrations of 3D objects, line drawings, and human sketches to produce descriptors that have supe- rior performance compared to other view-based or 3D shape descriptors in a variety of setups. Furthermore, they are compact and efﬁcient to compute. There has been existing work on recognizing 3D objects with CNNs [21] using two concatenated views (binocular images) as input. Our net- work instead learns a shape representation that aggregates information from any number of input views without any speciﬁc ordering, and always outputs a compact shape de- scriptor of the same size. Furthermore, we leverage both image and shape datasets to train our network. Although there is signiﬁcant work...

In contrast our multi-view CNN architecture learns to recognize 3D shapes from views of the shapes using image-based CNNs but in the context of other views via a view-pooling layer. As a result, information from multiple views is effectively accu- mulated into a single, compact shape descriptor. 3. Method As discussed above, our focus in this paper is on devel- oping view-based descriptors for 3D shapes that are train- able, produce informative representations for recognition and retrieval tasks, and are efﬁcient to compute. Our view-based representations start from multiple views of a 3D shape, generated by a rendering engine. A simple way to use multiple views is to generate a 2D image descriptor per each view, and then use the individual de- scriptors directly for recognition tasks based on some vot- ing or alignment scheme. Com- pared to exhaustive pairwise comparisons between single- view representations of 3D shapes, our resulting descriptors can be directly used to compare 3D shapes leading to sig- niﬁcantly higher computational efﬁciency. 3.1. Input: A Multi-view Representation 3D models in online databases are typically stored as polygon meshes, which are collections of points connected
with edges forming faces. To generate rendered views of
polygon meshes, we use the Phong reﬂection model [27]. The mesh polygons are rendered under a perspective pro-
jection and the pixel color is determined by interpolating

the reﬂected intensity of the polygon vertices. Shapes are uniformly scaled to ﬁt into the viewing volume. To create a multi-view shape representation, we need to setup viewpoints (virtual cameras) for rendering each mesh.

We experimented with two camera setups. Forthe 1st cam- era setup, we assume that the input shapes are upright ori- ented along a consistent axis (e.g., z-axis). Most models in modern online repositories, such as the 3D Warehouse, sat- isfy this requirement, and some previous recognition meth- ods also follow the same assumption [37]. In this case, we create 12 rendered views by placing 12 virtual cameras around the mesh every 30 degrees (see Fig. 1). The cameras are elevated 30 degrees from the ground plane, pointing to- wards the centroid of the mesh. The centroid is calculated as the weighted average of the mesh face centers, where the weights are the face areas. For the 2nd camera setup, we do not make use of the assumption about consistent up- right orientation of shapes. In this case, we render from several more viewpoints since we do not know beforehand which ones yield good representative views of the object. The renderings are generated by placing 20 virtual cameras at the 20...

due to the invariance of the learned ﬁlters to illumination

changes, as also observed in image-based CNNs [20, 10]. Adding more or different viewpoints is trivial, however, we found that the above camera setups were already enough to achieve high performance. Finally, rendering each mesh from all the viewpoints takes no more than ten milliseconds on modern graphics hardware. 3.2. Recognition with Multi-view Representations We claim that our multi-view representation contains rich information about 3D shapes and can be applied to var- ious types of tasks. In the ﬁrst setting, we make use of ex- isting 2D image features directly and produce a descriptor for each view. This is the most straightforward approach to utilize the multi-view representation. However, it results in multiple 2D image descriptors per 3D shape, one per view, which need to be integrated somehow for recognition tasks. Image descriptors. We consider two types of image de- scriptors for each 2D view: a state-of-the-art “hand-crafted” image descriptor based on Fisher vectors [29...
and a softmax classiﬁcation layer. The penultimate layer

fc7 (after ReLU non-linearity, 4096-dimensional) is used as image descriptor. The network is pre-trained on Ima- geNet images from 1k categories, and then ﬁne-tuned on all 2D views of the 3D shapes in training set. As we show in our experiments, ﬁne-tuning improves performance signif- icantly. Both Fisher vectors and CNN features yield very good performance in classiﬁcation and retrieval compared with popular 3D shape descriptors (e.g., SPH [16], LFD [5]) as well as 3D ShapeNets [37]. Classiﬁcation. We train one-vs-rest linear SVMs (each view is treated as a separate training sample) to classify shapes using their image features. At test time, we simply sum up the SVM decision values over all 12 views and re- turn the class with the highest sum. Alternative approaches, e.g., averaging image descriptors, lead to worse accuracy. Retrieval. A distance or similarity measure is required for retrieval tasks. We design the multi-view CNN (MVCNN) on top of image-based CNNs (Fig. 1). Each image in a 3D shape’s multi-view representation is passed through the ﬁrst part of the network (CNN 1) separately, aggregated at a view- pooling layer, and then sent through the remaining part of the network (CNN 2). All branches in the ﬁrst part of the network share the same parameters in CNN 1. We use
element-wise maximum operation across the views in the

view-pooling layer. An alternative is element-wise mean operation, but it is not as effective in our experiments. The view-pooling layer can be placed anywhere in the network. We show in our experiments that it should be placed close to the last convolutional layer (conv 5) for optimal classiﬁ- cation and retrieval performance. View-pooling layers are
closely related to max-pooling layers and maxout layers

[14], with the only difference being the dimension that their pooling operations are carried out on. The MVCNN is a di- rected acyclic graphs and can be trained or ﬁne-tuned using stochastic gradient descent with back-propagation. Using fc 7 (after ReLU non-linearity) in an MVCNN as an aggregated shape descriptor, we achieve higher per- formance than using separate image descriptors from an image-based CNN directly, especially in retrieval (62.8% → 70.1%). Perhaps more importantly, the aggregated de- scriptor is readily available for a variety of tasks,e.g., shape classiﬁcation and retrieval, and offers signiﬁcant speed-ups against multiple image descriptors. An MVCNN can also be used as a general framework to integrate perturbed image samples (also known as data jittering). We illustrate this capability of MVCNNs in the context of sketch recognition in Sect. 4.2. Low-rank Mahalanobis metric. gregating multiple views of a 2D image could also improve performance. Here we show that this is indeed the case by exploring its connection with data jittering in the context of sketch recognition. Data jittering, or data augmentation, is a method to gen- erate extra samples from a given image. It is the process of perturbing the image by transformations that change its appearance while leaving the high-level information (class

In particular, several authors [20, 3, 35] have used data jittering to improve the performance of deep representations on 2D image classiﬁcation tasks. In these applications, jittering at training time usually includes random image translations (implemented as random crops), horizontal reﬂections, and color perturbations. At test time jittering usually only in- cludes a few crops (e.g., four at the corners, one at the center
and their horizontal reﬂections). We now examine whether

we can get more beneﬁt out of jittered views of an image by using the same feature aggregation scheme we developed for recognizing 3D shapes. The human sketch dataset [11] contains 20,000 hand- drawn sketches of 250 object categories such as airplanes, apples, bridges, etc. The accuracy of humans in recogniz- ing these hand-drawings is only 73% because of the low quality of some sketches. Schneider and Tuytelaars [30] cleaned up the dataset by removing instances and categories that humans ﬁnd hard to recognize. This cleaned dataset (SketchClean) contains 160 categories, on which humans can achieve 93% recognition accuracy. Using SIFT Fisher vectors with spatial pyramid pooling and linear SVMs, Schneider and Tuytelaars achieved 68.9% recognition accu- racy on the original dataset and 79.0% on the SketchClean dataset. Conclusion While the world is full of 3D shapes, as humans at least, we understand that world is mostly through 2D images. We query top 10 retrieved 3D shapes

While even a n ¨aive usage of these multiple 2D pro-
jections yields impressive discrimination performance, by

building descriptors that are aggregations of information from multiple views, we can achieve compactness, efﬁ- ciency, and better accuracy. In addition, by relating the content of 3D shapes to 2D representations like sketches, we can retrieve these 3D shapes at high accuracy using sketches, and leverage the implicit knowledge of 3D shapes contained in their 2D views. There are a number of directions to explore in future work. One is to experiment with different combinations of 2D views. Which views are most informative? How many views are necessary for a given level of accuracy? Can in- formative views be selected on the ﬂy? Another obvious question is whether our view aggregat- ing techniques can be used for building compact and dis-
criminative descriptors for real-world 3D objects from mul-

tiple views, or automatically from video, rather than merely for 3D polygon mesh models. Such investigations could be immediately applicable to widely studied problems such as object recognition and face recognition. Acknowledgements We thank Yanjie Li for her help on rendering meshes.
